primary_authorities_used: FBI IC3 Private Industry Notification 220420-2, "Ransomware Attacks on Agricultural Cooperatives Potentially Timed to Critical Seasons" (Apr 20, 2022) - https://www.ic3.gov/CSA/2022/220420-2.pdf

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Grain contracts are settled by wire transfer based on emailed payment instructions.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Soybeans are sold on cash, basis, and hedge-to-arrive contracts. Contract confirmations, scale tickets, and remittance advices are sent by email. An attacker with access to the farm's or the elevator's email account can send a fake change of bank account. The farm then authorizes the wire itself.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: One truckload settlement is $15,000 to $40,000. A full contract settlement is $250,000 or more. Banks rarely recover a wire after 24 hours. Crime policies generally exclude transfers the insured authorized, so the loss falls under cyber social engineering coverage or nowhere.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you receive payment or banking instructions from grain buyers by email?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Planting and harvest data is stored in cloud accounts that have known vulnerabilities.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Seeding prescriptions, RTK guidance, section control settings, and yield maps are stored in John Deere Operations Center, Climate FieldView, or Trimble Ag. In-cab displays sync to those accounts over cellular. In 2021 security researchers demonstrated flaws in Deere's API that allowed owner enumeration and administrative access to Operations Center.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Loss of account access during a 10 to 14 day planting window forces flat-rate seeding and manual passes. Yield history used for crop insurance APH, landlord negotiations, and seed decisions is also lost.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you store field maps, prescriptions, or yield data in a cloud platform such as Operations Center or FieldView?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: A ransomware attack on your elevator stops your deliveries with no damage to your property.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: The FBI issued a notice in April 2022 stating that ransomware actors time attacks on agricultural cooperatives to planting and harvest. Six grain cooperatives were encrypted between September 15 and October 6, 2021. When an elevator's scale, probe, and settlement software is down, it cannot receive grain.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Two weeks of blocked delivery during harvest with limited on-farm storage. Farm and property policies respond only to physical damage to covered property, so a buyer's system outage is not covered. Contingent business interruption under a cyber policy is the coverage that applies.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: How many elevators or processors can you deliver to within economical hauling distance?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Production is contracted to a small number of crush plants with scheduled delivery slots.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Canola, sunflower, flax, and safflower are grown on production contracts. Delivery slots are scheduled electronically. Act-of-God clauses cover weather but not a buyer's system failure. There is limited spot market depth to absorb production if the crusher cannot receive.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Missed delivery windows require a contract buyout or a discounted distressed sale. Property policies do not respond because nothing was physically damaged.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Is your crop sold under contract to a single processor?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Fall input prepay is made in a small number of large wire transfers.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Seed, fertilizer, and chemical are prepaid in the fall for pricing and tax reasons. Payment is usually one wire to a retailer or cooperative against an invoice received by email. Attackers alter the account details on a real invoice.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: A prepay wire of $150,000 to $400,000 sent to a criminal account. The supplier has not been paid and still expects payment, so the operation pays twice.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you prepay inputs by wire transfer, and what is the largest single payment you make in a year?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Identity-preserved premiums depend on documentation you must produce on demand.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: High-oleic and specialty oilseed contracts are identity-preserved. The grower must document seed lot, field isolation, field history, and segregated handling. These records are kept in spreadsheets or a grower portal. Without them the crop is graded as commodity.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: An identity-preserved premium of $0.60 to $2.00 per bushel is lost across the contracted acreage because the documentation chain cannot be produced for the buyer's auditor.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you grow any crop under an identity-preserved or specialty contract that requires recordkeeping?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Export shipments require electronic certificates that must match the cargo.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: A large share of US pulses is exported. Shipments require electronic phytosanitary certificates issued through USDA APHIS PCIT, certificates of origin, and buyer quality documentation. Destination countries set different maximum residue limits, which are verified against your spray records.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: A container arriving without matching documentation is detained and often rejected. Demurrage runs $150 to $300 per container per day before the cargo itself is addressed.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you export any portion of your crop, and do you maintain the pesticide application records used for residue compliance?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Contracts settle by wire to processors and brokers you deal with infrequently.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Dry edible bean and pulse marketing runs through a limited number of processors and brokers, often out of state. Communication is by email. There is no regular in-person contact with the accounting staff who send remittance advices, which removes the check that would catch an altered account number.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: A diverted settlement wire of $80,000 to $300,000 on a single contract.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you sell to out-of-state buyers you have not met in person?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Certified seed status depends on lot records kept on the farm.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Certified pulse seed carries variety protection and certification tags administered by state crop improvement associations. Lot traceability is required to sell seed as certified. The records are digital and are frequently stored only on the farm office computer.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Loss of certification status drops certified seed value to commodity value across the affected lots.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you produce certified seed, and where are your lot and certification records stored?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Custom harvest is coordinated through cloud software across multiple states.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Wheat harvest moves north from Texas to Montana. Field locations, acres, moisture readings, machine telematics, and per-acre billing are coordinated between grower and custom cutter through cloud platforms and mobile devices. When that coordination fails, machines and crews stop.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Idle custom harvest equipment and crew costs $8,000 to $15,000 per day. Standing wheat left through a weather event suffers shattering, sprout damage, and falling number discounts across the field.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you use a custom harvest crew, and how is field and acre information shared with them?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Premiums and discounts are calculated from grade data held by the buyer.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Wheat settles on protein, test weight, falling number, and dockage. These are measured at the elevator and recorded in the elevator's system. The grower does not hold an independent copy. Disputes are resolved from the buyer's records.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: A 40 cent protein premium on 60,000 bushels is $24,000. If the buyer's records are encrypted or unavailable, there is no basis to support a claim for that amount.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you keep your own copy of scale tickets and grade sheets from your buyer?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Crop insurance claims have deadlines that a systems outage does not extend.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Federal crop insurance requires acreage reports by the acreage reporting date, notice of loss generally within 72 hours of discovery, and production records to support an APH claim. These records are held in farm management software and FSA and RMA portals.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: A denied or reduced indemnity in a claim year. Wheat coverage commonly runs $80,000 to $250,000 on a mid-size operation.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you carry federal crop insurance, and how are your production and acreage records stored?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Grain dryers are network connected and run unattended at high temperature.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: GSI, Sukup, and Mathews continuous-flow dryers ship with remote monitoring and control of plenum temperature, moisture setpoint, and discharge rate. Corn enters at 22 to 25 percent moisture and is dried at 180 to 220 degrees F. The dryer runs around the clock during harvest and is frequently monitored by phone.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: A dryer fire destroys the dryer and adjacent bins. Replacement cost is $150,000 to $500,000 before the value of the grain. Incorrect drying causes stress cracks and damage discounts across all grain that passed through.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Is your grain dryer or bin monitoring system accessible remotely from a phone or computer?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Corn carries the largest input prepay of any row crop.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Nitrogen, seed, and chemical prepay is concentrated into a few large payments to cooperatives and retailers, arranged by email. The FBI notice of April 2022 specifically identified attacks on cooperatives that supply seed and fertilizer ahead of planting.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: A diverted prepay wire of $200,000 to $800,000. The fertilizer was never booked, so the operation buys nitrogen again at spring spot price on top of the stolen funds.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: What is the dollar amount of your largest input prepayment, and how is it sent?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Corn production depends on hybrid-specific data stored in cloud accounts.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Variable-rate population, multi-hybrid planting, downforce maps, RTK guidance, and as-applied records are stored in Operations Center or FieldView. Researchers demonstrated in 2021 that Deere's platform allowed owner enumeration and administrative access.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: A season planted at flat rate, plus permanent loss of multi-year yield history used for seed selection, cash rent negotiation, and crop insurance APH.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: How many years of yield data do you have stored, and is there a copy outside the cloud account?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Flood management depends on pumps and gates that are controlled remotely.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Rice is grown under a managed flood held for months. Relift pumps, wells, and multiple-inlet gates are increasingly controlled by cell telemetry and phone apps. Loss of the flood at certain growth stages causes blanking and weed escape.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: An uncontrolled drain or a failure to restart pumps during a heat event across 400 acres is a partial or total loss on that acreage with no replant option.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Are any of your irrigation pumps or water control gates operated remotely?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Drying and milling are done off-farm and determine the value of the crop.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Rice is harvested at 18 to 20 percent moisture and must be dried quickly. Delivery scheduling, drying charges, and milling yield are handled in the drier's or mill's software. Head rice percentage determines the payment.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Rice held wet because the drier cannot receive it loses head rice yield permanently. A five point drop in head rice across a crop is a six figure loss with no physical damage to farm property.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you rely on a single drier or mill to receive your crop at harvest?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Program payments and insurance depend on federal records tied to deadlines.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Base acres, ARC and PLC elections, FSA farm records, and crop insurance APH are held in electronic records with filing deadlines. Rice also carries residue documentation for domestic and export buyers.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Missed FSA or RMA deadlines and unsupported APH history reduce both program payments and insurance guarantees in future years, not only the current year.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you participate in FSA programs and federal crop insurance?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Two crops means payment and contract activity across roughly eight months.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: A combination operation markets corn and soybeans to different buyers under different contract structures. Delivery and settlement run from September through the following summer. Email traffic about contracts, delivery, and payment is active most of the year.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Diverted settlement or prepay wires of $50,000 to $500,000 per event. A compromised mailbox is typically used more than once before the pattern is detected.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: In how many months of the year do you send or receive payments over $50,000?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Combination operations are heavy users of farm management software.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Rotating corn and soybeans across many fields and landlords requires field records, rotation history, variable-rate prescriptions, and landlord-by-landlord accounting. This is held in Operations Center, FieldView, Granular, or similar cloud platforms accessed with a single set of credentials.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Loss of multi-year rotation and yield history used to support cash rent negotiations and landlord reporting.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: How many landlords do you report field results to, and where is that data kept?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Annual operating lines require financial documents sent electronically to lenders.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Large grain operations renew operating notes annually on financial statements, inventory positions, and marketing plans. Tax returns, balance sheets, and bank account details are submitted through lender portals or by email and remain in the sent folder.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Loan renewal delayed because financials cannot be produced, plus account takeover using the financial documents recovered from a compromised mailbox.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you send tax returns or financial statements to your lender by email?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Specialty grain premiums are conditional on contract documentation.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Barley, oats, sorghum, rye, and specialty grains are grown on contract to maltsters, millers, and feed buyers. Contracts specify protein, plumpness, germination, test weight, and DON limits. The premium is paid only when the specification documentation is produced.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: A malting barley contract paying $2 to $4 over feed barley reverts to feed value across the contracted volume.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you sell any grain under a specification contract that pays a premium over commodity price?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Specialty grains often have only one buyer within hauling distance.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Unlike corn and soybeans, small grains and specialty grains frequently have a single realistic buyer in the area. The FBI documented multiple grain cooperatives encrypted within a three week window during the 2021 harvest.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Grain with no delivery point during harvest and limited on-farm storage, forcing a distressed sale or ground storage losses.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: How many buyers will take this crop within your normal hauling distance?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Breach notification law applies to farms of any size.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Any farm with employees holds W-2 data, direct deposit routing numbers, and I-9 forms. Many also hold H-2A documentation. All 50 states require notification when personal information is breached. There is no exemption based on revenue or number of employees.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Forensics, required notification, credit monitoring, and state attorney general response cost $25,000 to $100,000 for a small employer before any lawsuit.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: How many employees do you hold Social Security numbers and direct deposit information for?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Potato storage is run by ventilation controllers that are monitored remotely.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Potatoes are stored 6 to 10 months under controlled pile temperature, humidity, CO2, and airflow. Controllers from Gellert, Industrial Ventilation, and Techmark are used and are usually monitored and adjusted remotely. Pile temperature must be held within a few degrees. Sprout inhibitor application and CO2 levels are also controlled.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: A 30 million pound storage building holds $2M to $4M of potatoes. A controller failure or loss of monitoring access causes pressure bruise, pit rot, or blackheart across the pile.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Are your storage ventilation controls monitored or adjusted remotely?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Processor contracts are transacted by EDI on fixed delivery schedules.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Contract potatoes are delivered to Lamb Weston, McCain, Simplot, or a chip plant. Delivery slots, quality specifications, and payment are transmitted electronically. Sugar and specific gravity results are held in the processor's system.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Missed delivery windows and unresolved quality settlements. If the processor is down and cannot receive, the grower has no delivery point and no coverage under a property policy.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: What percentage of your crop is committed to a single processor?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Seed potato certification depends on lot and testing records.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Seed lot certification, virus and blackleg testing, and field inspection results determine whether seed can legally be sold. Records are held by state certification agencies and by the grower.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Loss of certified status converts seed value to table stock value. If a buyer's crop fails, downstream claims are made against the seed grower who cannot document lot history.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you sell certified seed potatoes to other growers?

111219.naics_title: Other Vegetable (except Potato) and Melon Farming

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Your crops are on the FDA Food Traceability List and require records within 24 hours.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Melons, leafy greens, tomatoes, cucumbers, peppers, fresh herbs, and sprouts are on the FDA Food Traceability List under FSMA Section 204. The compliance date is July 20, 2028. The rule requires traceability lot codes, Key Data Elements at Critical Tracking Events, and delivery of records to FDA in an electronic sortable spreadsheet within 24 hours of request.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Records that cannot be produced in 24 hours widen the scope of an outbreak investigation. The 2018 romaine advisories reduced demand for growers who were never linked to the outbreak.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you grow any crop on the FDA Food Traceability List, and can you produce lot-level records electronically?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Retail buyers require EDI, GS1 labeling, and a current third-party food safety audit.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Selling to retailers or foodservice distributors requires GTINs, case labeling, EDI purchase orders and advance ship notices, and a current PrimusGFS, SQF, or GlobalG.A.P. certificate held in a portal. Product cannot ship without electronic confirmation, and the certificate is checked before orders are placed.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Suspension from an approved supplier list during the harvest season. Perishable product cannot be held until the issue is resolved.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you transmit purchase orders or advance ship notices by EDI to your buyers?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Seasonal harvest crews create a large file of employee personal information.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Fresh vegetable production uses large seasonal crews, employed directly or through a farm labor contractor. Files include I-9 forms, passport and visa copies, Social Security numbers, and direct deposit details. Payroll is run weekly.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: A breach of a payroll file covering 400 workers requires notification in every state of residence, credit monitoring, and response to state labor agencies.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: How many seasonal employees do you have at peak, and do you keep copies of their identity documents?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Freeze protection uses pumps and wind machines that are started remotely.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Citrus is protected from freeze events by microsprinkler irrigation and wind machines. These are started based on remote temperature telemetry and are controlled by app or SCADA, usually overnight. The decision window is under an hour.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: One unprotected freeze night destroys the fruit crop and can kill young trees. Grove replanting costs $8,000 to $15,000 per acre and takes 4 to 7 years to return to production.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Are your frost protection pumps or wind machines started or monitored remotely?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Greening management is run from multi-year block-level records.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: HLB, or citrus greening, is managed through tree-by-tree nutrition programs, psyllid scouting maps, injection records, and multi-year block yield and mortality data. This data is held in grove management software and directs the treatment program.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Loss of block records requires restarting the nutrition and psyllid program without historical reference on a disease that kills trees faster than the data can be rebuilt.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you use grove management software to track block-level treatment and yield history?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Payment is calculated from pound solids measured in the processor's laboratory.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Processing oranges are paid on pound solids, determined by Brix and juice yield measured at the processor and recorded in the processor's system. Fresh fruit is paid on packout percentage calculated at the packinghouse. The grower has no independent measurement.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Unresolved settlement across a season. If the processor cannot receive fruit, there is no alternative outlet for a perishable crop that cannot be held on the tree.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Is your payment based on grade or yield data generated by the buyer?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Frost protection for high-value citrus is automated and remotely controlled.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Lemons, grapefruit, mandarins, and limes are freeze sensitive and are protected by remotely controlled microsprinkler and wind machine systems. Per-acre values are higher than oranges. Mandarin acreage in particular carries high revenue per acre.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Total crop loss on acreage grossing $8,000 to $20,000 per acre, plus tree damage on varieties with long establishment periods.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Are your frost protection systems operated remotely, and what is your revenue per acre?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Club and managed varieties require reporting through a grower portal.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Managed and club citrus varieties require licensed plantings, reported acreage, quality compliance, and marketing through one designated handler. Compliance is administered through grower portals. The license is what permits the fruit to be sold under the brand.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: License compliance failure or inability to report during harvest sends fruit into the generic market at a fraction of branded value.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you grow any licensed or club variety that requires reporting to a handler?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Export requires electronic phytosanitary certificates and residue documentation.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Specialty citrus exported to Japan, Korea, Canada, and the EU requires phytosanitary certificates issued through APHIS PCIT, cold treatment records, and compliance with destination maximum residue limits. Compliance is verified against your spray records. Permitted chemistries differ by country.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Container detention or rejection on perishable product, and removal from an export program that took years to qualify for.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you export fruit, and do you maintain electronic spray and treatment records?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Controlled atmosphere storage holds fruit under continuous computer control for months.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Apples are stored at 1.5 to 2.5 percent oxygen and 1 to 3 percent CO2 for up to ten months. Dynamic controlled atmosphere systems monitor and adjust continuously. Rooms are sealed. Fruit held below the lower oxygen limit ferments and CO2 excursions cause internal browning. These systems are networked for remote monitoring.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: One CA room holds 100,000 to 200,000 bushels, worth $1M to $3M. A control failure or loss of monitoring access can make the entire room unsellable, and the damage is not visible until the room is opened months later.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you operate controlled atmosphere storage, and is it monitored remotely?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Shipping to retail requires packinghouse grading data, GS1 labeling, and EDI.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Apples reach retail through optical grading, case labeling, PLU assignment, and EDI order processing. Presize grading data determines packout and payment. There is no manual process for shipping to a national retailer.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Shipping stops during a retail promotion window while fruit continues to age in storage.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you ship to national retail chains that require EDI?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Fall retail and u-pick operations process a high volume of card transactions.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Most orchards run retail operations in the fall, including u-pick, farm markets, cider sales, and ticketed events. Card transactions are concentrated into roughly eight weekends across POS systems and online ticketing. PCI DSS 4.0 requirements became mandatory on March 31, 2025 and apply regardless of merchant size.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Card brand assessments, forensic investigation, and card reissuance costs after a POS or e-commerce compromise. PCI liability is excluded or sublimited on most package policies.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you accept credit cards at a farm market, u-pick, or online store?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Wine club billing stores customer card data for recurring charges.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Vineyards with winery operations run wine clubs that store customer cards for quarterly billing. Tasting room POS, e-commerce, and shipping compliance records add names, addresses, and dates of birth for age verification. This is stored payment data combined with personal information for thousands of customers.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: A club database breach exposes stored cards for 3,000 to 15,000 members. Costs include notification, card brand assessments, forensics, and loss of the customer list.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you store customer credit card information for recurring or club billing?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Frost protection, irrigation, and pick timing are driven by remote sensor data.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Vineyards use remotely monitored frost alarms, wind machines, overhead sprinklers, and soil moisture probes. Brix sampling determines pick date within roughly a 48 hour window. Frost alarms are acted on overnight.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: A missed frost event at bud break destroys the primary crop for the season. A mistimed pick moves fruit outside the target Brix and pH range and moves the lot from reserve tier to bulk.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you rely on remote frost alarms or sensor data to make overnight decisions?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Label claims must be substantiated with records that TTB can audit.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Vintage, varietal, appellation, and vineyard designate claims must be supported by records available for TTB audit. Vineyards supplying wineries must document block, tonnage, and delivery to support those claims. Weight tags and lot records are the supporting evidence.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Inability to substantiate label claims in an audit requires relabeling or destruction of bottled inventory, plus contractual liability to wineries relying on your records.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you supply fruit for vineyard-designate or appellation labeling?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Strawberries require continuous cold chain monitoring and have a five day shelf life.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Berries move from field to forced-air precooling within about an hour and must hold 32 to 34 degrees F through to retail. Precooling tunnels, cold rooms, and refrigerated transport are monitored by networked temperature loggers. Buyers reject loads based on temperature data alone.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: A cooling or monitoring failure on one day's harvest of 3,000 to 8,000 flats is a total write-off within 48 hours. There is no salvage market.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you use networked temperature monitoring in your coolers or shipping?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Hand harvest generates weekly payroll and piece-rate records for a large crew.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Strawberries are harvested by hand at piece rate using hundreds of workers, often through H-2A or a farm labor contractor. Files include I-9 forms, visa documents, and direct deposit information. Piece-rate and hours records are legally required in California and Florida.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Breach notification across a large seasonal workforce. In a wage claim, an employer who cannot produce time and pay records faces a legal presumption in favor of the employee's estimate.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: How do you record and store piece-rate and hours worked for your harvest crew?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Outbreak traceback is conducted using lot codes and harvest records.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Fresh strawberries were the subject of a multistate hepatitis A outbreak investigation in 2022 that publicly named brands and growing regions. Traceback uses lot codes, harvest records, and distribution data. Slow or unavailable records extend the investigation and widen the public advisory.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: A regional advisory reduces demand for every grower in the district. Recall expense, crisis management, and public relations costs are covered under cyber and recall policies, not farm property policies.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Can you trace a specific lot from field to buyer using your current records?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Optical sorting determines whether fruit is sold fresh or for processing.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Fresh blueberries are graded by optical and near-infrared sorters that log packout by lot. Fresh pack value is commonly two to three times processing value. The sorter determines which market the fruit enters. Cold chain is monitored continuously after packing.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: A sorting or cold chain outage during a two week peak diverts fresh market fruit to processing at a much lower price, or writes off cane berries that will not hold.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you operate optical sorting or automated packing equipment?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Direct sales channels make the operation a card-accepting merchant.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Berry growers sell through u-pick, farmers markets, roadside stands, CSA subscriptions, and online ordering using mobile POS and e-commerce platforms. PCI DSS 4.0 became fully mandatory on March 31, 2025 and includes e-commerce script controls.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Card brand fines and forensic costs after a POS compromise, plus contractual liability to the acquiring bank. This liability is excluded under a BOP or farmowners policy.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you accept credit cards in person, online, or both?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Buyer programs require a current certification verified through a portal.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Berries sold to national retailers and export markets require GlobalG.A.P., PrimusGFS, or SQF certification, harvest and spray records, and residue documentation. Certification status is verified through cloud portals before orders are placed.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Loss of approved supplier status during harvest, with perishable product and no time to re-qualify.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Which third-party food safety certifications do you hold, and where are the records kept?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Truckloads of nuts are stolen using compromised or fake carrier identities.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Almond, pistachio, and walnut loads are stolen by criminals who compromise or impersonate carrier and broker accounts on load boards, produce matching pickup documentation, and collect the load. The product is high value, non-perishable, and difficult to trace after resale. This is an established pattern targeting California tree nuts.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: One truckload of almonds or pistachios is $150,000 to $500,000. Because the goods were released voluntarily to a party presenting valid-looking documents, this is generally not covered as a property theft loss.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: How do you verify the identity of a carrier before releasing a load?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Irrigation is controlled by SCADA and remote pump control on a permanent crop.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Tree nuts are permanent crops with high water demand, irrigated through pressurized microirrigation with remote pump control, flow monitoring, and soil moisture telemetry. Groundwater use is reported under SGMA in California. Orchards take 7 to 10 years to reach full production.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Extended irrigation loss during summer heat kills or permanently damages trees. Almond orchard establishment costs $8,000 to $12,000 per acre and takes about 7 years to return to production.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Are your irrigation pumps controlled or monitored through a remote system?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Payment is made by handlers over 12 to 18 months against their grade data.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Tree nuts are delivered to handlers who pool, market, and pay over an extended period based on grade sheets, moisture, and reject data generated in the handler's system. About two thirds of US tree nuts are exported, requiring APHIS phytosanitary certification and aflatoxin testing documentation.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Delayed pool payments and inability to export product already in the warehouse. On a crop paid out over 18 months, a settlement system failure creates a cash flow shortfall.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Over what period are you paid for your crop after delivery?

111336.naics_title: Fruit and Tree Nut Combination Farming

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Multiple crops extend the critical operating window across most of the year.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: A combination operation harvests, packs, cools, and ships across most of the year, with different buyers, food safety schemes, labor peaks, and settlement systems for each commodity. There is no period in which a systems outage falls outside a harvest window.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: An outage at any point in an eight to ten month operating window occurs during an active harvest with perishable product on the tree or in the cooler.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: In how many months of the year are you actively harvesting or shipping?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Permanent plantings are destroyed, not just interrupted, by irrigation failure.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Orchards and vineyards have 15 to 40 year productive lives and multi-year establishment periods. They depend on remotely controlled irrigation and frost protection. Unlike annual crops, production cannot be resumed the following season.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Tree or vine mortality from extended irrigation or freeze protection failure requires replanting at $8,000 to $20,000 per acre with 4 to 8 years to full production.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: What is the replanting cost per acre for your orchard or vineyard blocks?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Mixed commodities multiply traceability and certification requirements on shared systems.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Combination operations often grow crops on the FDA Food Traceability List alongside crops that are not covered, plus commodities with export residue restrictions. Each requires separate lot coding, records, and certification. FSMA 204 applies to the covered items on July 20, 2028 regardless of the other crops grown.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: A single records failure affects every commodity because the systems are shared, satisfying neither a traceback investigator nor a certification auditor.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you keep records for all of your crops in the same system?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Tropical tree fruits are on the FDA Food Traceability List.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Papaya, mango, and other tropical tree fruits are covered by FSMA Section 204, with a compliance date of July 20, 2028. The rule requires traceability lot codes, Key Data Elements at Critical Tracking Events, and delivery of an electronic sortable spreadsheet to FDA within 24 hours of request. Papaya has a documented outbreak history.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Records that cannot be produced within 24 hours widen the scope of a traceback and place the operation at the center of the advisory. Costs include recall expense, crisis management, and lost market access.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you grow papaya, mango, or another crop on the FDA Food Traceability List?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Stone fruit requires rapid cooling and continuous cold chain monitoring.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Peaches, nectarines, plums, cherries, and apricots require hydrocooling or forced-air cooling within hours of picking and continuous cold chain to retail. Cooling and transport are monitored electronically. Cherry harvest windows are measured in days.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: A cooling or monitoring failure writes off a full day of harvest. On cherries, one lost week can represent the majority of the crop's marketable value.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: How soon after picking does your fruit enter cooling, and is that process monitored electronically?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Fruit clubs and direct shipping involve stored card data and recurring billing.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Noncitrus fruit growers sell through u-pick, farm stands, fruit-of-the-month shipping clubs, and online ordering. Shipping clubs require stored cards and recurring billing. Farm stands process high transaction volume in a short season. PCI DSS 4.0 became mandatory on March 31, 2025.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Card compromise with brand assessments, forensics, and reissuance costs, plus loss of customers in a business built on direct relationships.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you operate a shipping club or subscription that stores customer cards?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Growing rooms and compost tunnels are under continuous computer control.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Mushroom production uses phase II and III composting tunnels held at set temperatures for pasteurization and conditioning, then growing rooms controlled for air temperature, compost temperature, humidity, CO2, and air exchange. Flushes are triggered by controlled environmental changes. The building supplies the entire growing environment.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Hours of lost environmental control aborts a flush and can contaminate the substrate. This costs the crop, the compost fill, and the room turn, commonly $50,000 to $200,000 per room. Rooms cycle every few weeks.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Are your growing room and tunnel controls accessible remotely?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Mushrooms have a documented Listeria recall history.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Enoki and other mushrooms have been subject to repeated multistate Listeria monocytogenes recalls and import alerts. Traceback uses lot codes, grow room records, and distribution data. Listeria is an environmental pathogen, so investigators review facility records in addition to product records.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Recall expense, destruction of distributed product, crisis management, and third-party bodily injury claims. Recall and crisis response costs are covered under cyber and recall policies, not farm property policies.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Can you identify which rooms and dates a specific shipment came from?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Hand harvest runs 52 weeks a year with continuous payroll.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Mushrooms are picked by hand indoors year round using large permanent and seasonal crews on piece rate. Unlike field crops, the employee file is active every week of the year and includes I-9 forms, Social Security numbers, and direct deposit details.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Breach notification across a large standing workforce, plus disruption to a weekly payroll with no seasonal pause to absorb the interruption.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: How many employees are on your payroll year round?

111419.naics_title: Other Food Crops Grown Under Cover

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: The greenhouse climate computer controls all growing conditions and allows remote access.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Greenhouse tomatoes, cucumbers, lettuce, and herbs are grown under Priva, Argus, Hoogendoorn, or Ridder climate computers. These control vents, screens, heating, CO2 dosing, supplemental lighting, and fertigation EC and pH. The systems are designed for remote monitoring and control by the grower and the vendor.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: A greenhouse without vent and screen control overheats within hours in summer or freezes in winter. Controlled environment sites commonly hold $2M to $20M in crop and infrastructure.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Does your climate control system allow remote access by you or your vendor?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Tomatoes, cucumbers, leafy greens, and herbs are on the FDA Food Traceability List.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: FSMA Section 204 covers the crops most commonly grown under cover. The compliance date is July 20, 2028. The rule requires traceability lot codes, Key Data Elements at Critical Tracking Events, and delivery of an electronic sortable spreadsheet to FDA within 24 hours of request.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Records that cannot be produced within 24 hours widen the scope of an outbreak investigation and result in product being pulled across the distribution chain.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Can you produce lot-level traceability records in an electronic spreadsheet format?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Retail supply agreements require year-round weekly volume.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Controlled environment operations sign year-round supply agreements with retailers specifying weekly volume, often backed by lender or investor covenants. The commitment is to a production schedule rather than a harvest. Downtime is a supply failure.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Breach of a year-round supply agreement, chargebacks or removal from a retail program, and lender covenant issues.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you have supply agreements that commit you to weekly delivery volumes?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Mail-order plant sales run through an e-commerce platform with a short selling season.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Nurseries sell direct to consumers online and ship live plants nationwide. Most annual revenue is earned in a six to ten week spring window. The operation runs a shopping cart, stored card data, and a customer database. PCI DSS 4.0 became mandatory on March 31, 2025 and added requirements for monitoring e-commerce payment page scripts.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: A cart compromise or ransomware event during the spring window affects the majority of annual revenue. Additional costs include card brand assessments, forensics, and customer notification across all states.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: What percentage of your annual sales occurs in your peak eight weeks, and do you sell online?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Interstate shipping requires state phytosanitary certification and quarantine compliance.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Shipping nursery stock across state lines requires state phytosanitary certification, nursery licenses, and compliance with quarantine orders for pests including sudden oak death, boxwood blight, emerald ash borer, and spotted lanternfly. Certificates and shipping records are electronic. Quarantine compliance requires documented origin and inspection history per shipment.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: A stop-sale order or shipping ban during the spring window while compliance cannot be documented, plus regulatory action if traceback fails during a pest investigation.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you ship nursery stock across state lines, and how are inspection and shipping records stored?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Container stock is watered by automated irrigation and dies quickly without it.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Container nursery stock holds very little water reserve and is irrigated by automated boom, overhead, and drip systems on timed and sensor-driven controllers. Many are remotely managed. In summer, container stock requires water daily or more often.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Two days without irrigation in summer kills container inventory representing one to five years of growing.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Is your irrigation controlled by an automated system, and is it monitored remotely?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Revenue is concentrated into fixed holiday dates that cannot be moved.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Cut flowers and potted crops are timed to Valentine's Day, Mother's Day, Easter, and Christmas. Crops are programmed months ahead to finish on an exact date and shipped against retail purchase orders through EDI. Product has no value after the holiday passes.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Missing a holiday window writes off crops grown over six months with no salvage value, plus retail chargebacks and possible loss of the program for the following year.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: What percentage of your annual revenue is tied to specific holiday delivery dates?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Flowering is controlled by photoperiod lighting and temperature schedules.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Floriculture requires precise day and night temperature differentials for height control, photoperiod lighting for flower initiation, and controlled fertigation EC and pH. These are managed by networked climate computers with remote access. A lighting schedule error can prevent flowering across an entire crop.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: A photoperiod or temperature control failure delays or prevents flowering on a crop programmed for a specific holiday. Fixed costs are already fully spent at that point.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Is your greenhouse lighting and temperature program controlled by a networked system?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Retail programs require EDI, barcode labeling, and vendor portal access.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Selling into mass-market retail requires EDI purchase orders and advance ship notices, UPC and case labeling, vendor-managed inventory reporting, and integration with the retailer's replenishment system. Vendors are measured on fill rate and on-time performance.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Vendor compliance chargebacks and program suspension. Retail floral programs are awarded annually, so a failed holiday affects the following year's contract.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you supply mass-market retailers under an EDI vendor program?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Selling leaf requires current certification held in a third-party database.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Major manufacturers and leaf merchants require participation in grower certification programs such as GAP Connections. These programs document labor practices, worker housing, training, and farm compliance. Certification status is verified before purchase.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Loss of certification standing or exposure of labor and housing data threatens the contract relationship, which is the only outlet for the crop.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Which grower certification programs are you enrolled in?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Tobacco uses H-2A labor and holds foreign worker identity documents.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Tobacco requires hand labor for transplanting, topping, priming, and housing, supplied largely through H-2A. Files include passports, visas, consular documentation, Social Security numbers, housing assignments, and weekly payroll records.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: A breach of an H-2A file triggers notification obligations and attention from the Department of Labor and plaintiff attorneys. Exposure of immigration documents creates direct harm to workers, which increases litigation exposure.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you employ H-2A workers, and do you retain copies of their passports or visas?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Curing barns run unattended on programmed temperature and humidity schedules.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Flue-cured tobacco is cured in bulk barns over roughly one week on programmed temperature and humidity schedules through yellowing, leaf drying, and stem drying. Barns are monitored by remote alarm and control systems. A barn that runs off schedule ruins the leaf inside it.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: A curing failure destroys the leaf in that barn with no recovery. Cured leaf value is roughly $2 to $3 per pound on a crop that is already fully invested.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Are your curing barns monitored by a remote alarm or control system?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Bale ownership is recorded in an electronic warehouse receipt system.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: US cotton is warehoused and traded using electronic warehouse receipts under the US Warehouse Act, administered through USDA-authorized providers and tied to Permanent Bale Identification numbers. The electronic receipt is the title document for the bale. The bales are stored off-site and the record of ownership is the account entry.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Fraudulent transfer of receipts or loss of account access during a price window. One module is roughly $30,000 to $45,000 and a full crop is commonly seven figures held in electronic title.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you hold electronic warehouse receipts, and who has access to that account?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Price is set bale by bale from USDA classing data delivered electronically.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Every US bale is classed by USDA AMS for micronaire, staple, strength, color grade, and leaf. Results are delivered electronically to the grower, the gin, and the merchant. Premiums and discounts against base price are applied from that data.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Inability to receive, verify, or dispute classing data across a crop. Premium and discount differences of several cents per pound total $50,000 to $150,000 on a mid-size operation.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: How do you receive and store your USDA classing results?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Module tracking, gin scheduling, and CCC loans all run on third-party systems.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Round modules are RFID tagged and tracked from field to gin. Gin scheduling determines when cotton is processed. CCC marketing assistance loans are entered and redeemed electronically against warehouse receipts through FSA.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Modules degrading in the field while the gin cannot schedule, plus loan and redemption timing problems that affect the price received.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you use CCC marketing assistance loans against your warehouse receipts?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Cane must be milled within 24 to 48 hours and one mill controls the schedule.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Sucrose inverts quickly after cutting, so cane must be milled within roughly one to two days. Growers deliver to a single mill or cooperative on daily quotas allocated electronically. There is no alternative buyer and no storage option.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Cut cane that cannot be delivered is a near-total loss on that tonnage within two days. A mill systems outage during grinding season is a contingent business interruption loss that farm property policies do not cover.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: How is your daily delivery quota communicated to you by the mill?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Payment is calculated from core sample analysis in the mill's laboratory.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Growers are paid on recoverable sugar per ton, determined by core sampling in the mill's lab and processed through the mill's accounting system. The grower has no independent measurement.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Unresolved payment disputes across a grinding season. A half point difference in recoverable sugar across 100,000 tons is a substantial six figure amount.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Is your payment calculated from sugar content measured by the mill?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Harvest requires continuous fleet dispatch and permitted field burning.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Cane harvest runs a continuous loop of harvesters, wagons, and highway trucks to the mill. Pre-harvest burn permits are issued and tracked by state agencies based on weather and smoke management conditions. Dispatch and permit documentation are electronic.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Fleet idle time of $10,000 to $25,000 per day, plus regulatory exposure if burn authorization and compliance records cannot be produced.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: How do you dispatch and track your harvest fleet during grinding season?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Hay is sold to remote buyers and is stolen through fraudulent pickup.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Hay is sold through online marketplaces, broker networks, and load boards to buyers the grower has not met, often across state lines. Fictitious pickup, where a criminal uses compromised or spoofed carrier credentials to collect a load, is an established freight fraud pattern.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: A stolen or unpaid load of premium alfalfa is $6,000 to $12,000 per truck. Organized operations take multiple loads before detection. Goods released to a fraudster are generally not covered as a property theft loss.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: How do you verify a buyer or carrier before releasing a load?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Export hay premiums depend on lab testing and certification documents.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Compressed alfalfa and timothy exported to Japan, Korea, China, and the Middle East require lab analysis for relative feed value, moisture, and nitrate, plus phytosanitary certification through APHIS PCIT and container-level documentation.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Loads held at port with daily demurrage, and export hay reverting to domestic feed value. The price difference commonly exceeds $60 to $100 per ton.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you sell into the export market, and where are your lab and certification records kept?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Baling moisture data prevents spontaneous combustion in stored hay.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Hay baled above safe moisture heats through microbial activity and can combust. Baler moisture sensors, preservative applicators, and stack temperature probes are used to prevent this, and readings are increasingly logged and transmitted.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: A hay fire destroys the stack, the barn, and adjacent equipment. Stored hay inventory for a commercial operation commonly represents $200,000 to $800,000.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you use moisture sensing or stack temperature monitoring on stored hay?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Growers are cooperative shareholders and the cooperative controls delivery and payment.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Sugar beet production runs through grower-owned cooperatives that allocate delivery by shares, schedule piling stations, operate tare labs, and pay in installments over the following year. The FBI notice of April 2022 identified agricultural cooperatives as targets during critical seasons and documented six grain cooperatives encrypted within three weeks.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Harvest delivery blocked during the fall window, plus disruption to a payment structure spread over 12 months or more. As a shareholder, the grower absorbs the cooperative's loss as well.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Are you a shareholder in the cooperative that receives and processes your crop?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Beets are stored in outdoor piles and paid on tare lab results.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Harvested beets are piled at receiving stations, ventilated to control pile temperature, and paid on sugar percentage and tare determined by laboratory sampling. Piles must be processed on a managed schedule or sugar content declines and rot spreads.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Delayed processing reduces recoverable sugar across the harvest. Inability to verify or dispute tare and sugar results affects payment on the full tonnage.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: How long is your crop held in piles before processing?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Sugar beets carry high per-acre input costs paid by wire.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Sugar beet production requires high spending per acre on seed, fungicide programs, irrigation, and specialized harvest equipment. Inputs are funded on operating credit and prepaid to suppliers by wire.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: A diverted input prepay wire of $150,000 to $500,000 against an operating line sized to the crop plan.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: What is your input cost per acre, and how are supplier prepayments sent?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Price is set by federal grading recorded electronically at the buying point.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Every load of farmer stock peanuts is officially graded by the Federal-State Inspection Service for kernel size, damage, foreign material, moisture, and segregation class. Results are entered electronically and determine contract price and CCC loan eligibility. A Segregation 2 or 3 classification substantially reduces load value.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Inability to receive, verify, or dispute grade results across a season on a crop where segregation class determines edible market price versus crush value.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: How do you receive and retain grade sheets from your buying point?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Aflatoxin traceback runs from the shelling plant back to the farm.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Peanuts are subject to FDA aflatoxin action levels and mandatory testing at shelling. Positive results are traced back to farmer stock lots using grade sheets and buying point records, then to specific fields and farms.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Product liability exposure where irrigation, harvest, drying, and storage records cannot be produced to support the grower's position in a traceback.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you maintain irrigation, drying, and storage records by field and lot?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Drying wagons run unattended for one to three days per load.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Farmer stock peanuts are dried with forced heated air under temperature limits. Excessive temperature causes off-flavor and splits. Insufficient drying causes mold and aflatoxin. Drying runs continuously for 24 to 72 hours per load, controlled automatically and increasingly monitored remotely across a large wagon fleet.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Damaged or moldy loads across a drying yard, converting edible grade peanuts to oil stock or condemned product. The value difference exceeds $500 per ton.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: How many drying wagons do you run at once, and how are they monitored?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Specialty crops are sold direct to consumers with stored card data.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: This category includes maple syrup, hops, culinary herbs, sod, and other specialty crops, most of which have a direct-to-consumer channel with online storefronts and subscription orders. Card data and customer records are held on the operation's systems. PCI DSS 4.0 became mandatory on March 31, 2025 and added e-commerce script controls.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Card compromise with brand assessments, forensics, and notification across all states of customer residence.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you sell direct to consumers online, and do you store customer payment information?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Maple sap collection depends on remote vacuum monitoring during a short season.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Maple production uses vacuum tubing networks across thousands of taps with electronic vacuum monitoring, leak detection, and reverse osmosis concentration. The season is four to six weeks. A vacuum leak reduces yield across a section and cannot be found by walking the lines daily.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Undetected vacuum loss across a section for a week during a short season reduces sap yield with no opportunity to recover it that year.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: How many taps do you operate, and do you use electronic vacuum monitoring?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Specialty premiums are conditional on contracts and certifications.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Hops are sold on multi-year contracts specifying variety, alpha acid, and lot certification. Organic, kosher, and specialty certifications require continuously maintained auditable records. Premiums over commodity value depend on documentation available on request.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Loss of certification or contract standing converts premium product to commodity value across a production year, commonly a 40 to 70 percent price reduction.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you hold organic or other certifications that require ongoing recordkeeping?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Cattle sales are settled by wire days after delivery.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Calves and feeders are sold through video auctions, order buyers, and private treaty. Settlement is by wire after delivery. Delivery instructions, weights, and payment details are exchanged by email between parties who transact once or twice a year.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: One load of calves is $80,000 to $150,000 and a large sale day can exceed $1M. Once the transfer is authorized, it is a deception loss rather than a covered theft, and banks rarely recover funds after 24 hours.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: How many times a year do you receive payment by wire, and what is the largest amount?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: USDA requires electronically readable identification for interstate cattle movement.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Effective November 5, 2024, APHIS requires official eartags on sexually intact cattle and bison 18 months and older, all dairy cattle, and rodeo and exhibition animals to be both visually and electronically readable for interstate movement. EID numbers are tied to premises IDs, health certificates, and movement records.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Inability to produce EID and movement records blocks interstate sale and shipment and prevents the operation from demonstrating compliance in a disease trace.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you move cattle across state lines, and how do you store your EID and movement records?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Remote water and monitoring systems cover ground that is not checked daily.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Extensive operations use remote water level and pump monitoring on tanks and wells, cellular and satellite telemetry, GPS collars, and remote gates across large acreage. In dry conditions cattle die within one to two days of losing water. Pastures may not be visited for several days.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Death loss from water failure in summer heat, discovered days late. Cattle values are commonly $2,000 or more per head. Farm policies do not cover losses caused by a control system failure.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you use remote monitoring for stock water or pasture equipment?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Custom yards hold cattle owned by others and maintain their records.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Custom feedlots feed cattle owned by investors, ranchers, and packers. Ownership records, feed billing, health treatment records, and closeout accounting are tracked by lot. The yard is a bailee responsible for the animals and for the records that establish ownership and performance.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Third-party liability to cattle owners for lost performance data, disputed closeouts, and inability to document ownership, plus liability for exposing owners' financial information. Farm policies do not cover third-party data liability.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: What percentage of the cattle in your yard are owned by customers rather than the yard?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Feed is formulated and delivered by computerized batching systems.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Feedlots use computerized batching and delivery systems such as Micro Technologies and Performance Beef to control ration formulation, mixing accuracy, and bunk calls twice daily. Cattle on high-concentrate finishing rations develop acidosis and bloat if feedings are missed or batches are wrong.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: A batching failure across a 20,000 head yard causes death loss and performance setback. Finished cattle are worth $2,200 to $2,800 per head, so a 1 percent death loss is approximately $500,000.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: What software do you use for ration formulation and feed delivery?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Yards move large amounts of money weekly by wire and ACH.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Feedlots purchase feeder cattle, sell finished cattle to packers, buy commodity feed, and maintain futures and options positions with brokers. Payment traffic is high in both frequency and value and is arranged by email.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Diverted purchase or settlement wires of $250,000 to $2M, or compromise of hedging account credentials resulting in unauthorized positions.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: How many wire transfers does your office send in a typical week?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Milking equipment is computer controlled and cows must be milked on schedule.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Robotic milking systems from Lely and DeLaval and automated rotary and parallel parlors control milking, teat prep, milk metering, conductivity-based mastitis detection, and cleaning cycles. Vendor remote access is standard. Cows must be milked two to three times daily. Unmilked cows develop mastitis and lose production.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Twenty-four hours of milking failure across a 1,000 cow herd causes clinical mastitis, permanent production loss for the lactation, and culling. Culled cows represent $2,000 to $3,500 each in addition to dumped milk.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Is your milking system computer controlled, and does your vendor have remote access?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Milk cooling is a regulated process and out-of-spec milk is rejected.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: The Grade A Pasteurized Milk Ordinance requires raw milk to be cooled to 45 degrees F or below within two hours of milking. Tank cooling, agitation, and clean-in-place cycles are automated and logged. The cooperative tests every pickup.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Rejected and dumped loads at $2,500 to $5,000 per tanker, possible loss of Grade A permit status, and antibiotic or bacteria count violations that suspend shipping.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Are your bulk tank temperature and CIP cycles logged automatically?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: All dairy cattle are covered by the federal electronic identification requirement.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: The APHIS rule effective November 5, 2024 requires all dairy cattle, regardless of age, to carry electronically readable official identification for interstate movement. DHIA herd records, individual production and health histories, breeding and genomic data, and cooperative quality records are also held electronically.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Loss of individual cow records affects breeding decisions, genomic value, and drug withdrawal tracking. A withdrawal tracking failure can result in an antibiotic residue violation.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: How do you track which cows are under a drug withdrawal period?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: The operation is subject to both milk regulation and cattle movement requirements.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Dual-purpose operations must meet Grade A milk regulation, cooling and CIP recordkeeping, and cooperative quality testing on the dairy side. They must also meet the APHIS electronic identification requirement effective November 5, 2024 for interstate cattle movement. Both regimes run on the same office systems.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: One systems failure creates simultaneous compliance failures in milk quality documentation and animal movement records, affecting both revenue streams at once.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Do you keep milk quality records and cattle movement records in the same system?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Milking, cooling, and feeding equipment are automated and time-critical.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Milking must occur on schedule to avoid mastitis and production loss. Milk must be cooled to 45 degrees F within two hours under the PMO. Feed mixing and delivery are computer controlled. All three run through networked systems with vendor remote access.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Simultaneous loss of milking, cooling, and feed control causes dumped milk, mastitis and culling losses, and nutritional setback across the herd.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: Which of your daily operations depend on automated control systems?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: The operation sells into several markets with separate payment channels.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Dual-purpose operations sell fluid milk to a cooperative, cull cows and bull calves to buyers, feeders to yards, and often breeding stock. Each has its own settlement process, and most are arranged by email.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: Diverted payments across multiple channels. A compromised mailbox is typically used across several transactions before the pattern is detected.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.rhetorical_question: How many different buyers pay you in a typical month?

reasons_ranked_by_importance.headline: Sealed barns depend on mechanical ventilation and animals die quickly without it.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.why_this_business: Finishing and sow barns are mechanically ventilated sealed buildings controlled by networked controllers with remote monitoring and alarms. Pigs generate substantial heat and have limited ability to regulate body temperature. A ventilation failure in warm weather causes mortality within about an hour.
reasons_ranked_by_importance.loss_scenario: A 2,400 head finishing barn represents roughly $250,000 to $400,000 in live animals. Multi-barn sites multiply the exposure. Additional costs include carcass disposal and cleanup.
